To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep neural networks with Gaussian weights and biases define Gaussian processes and converge weakly in function-space to continuous Gaussian processes in the large-width regime.
i) deep Gaussian networks define a Gaussian process in the function space; ii) in the large-width regime, the Gaussian process is continuous and has almost surely locally Hölder continuous paths.

i) deep Gaussian neural networks define continuous Gaussian processes on the input space; ii) deep Gaussian neural network with rescaled weights converges to the Gaussian process in the limit of infinite width.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: i) what is the functional asymptotic of infinitely wide deep Gaussian neural networks? ii) how does the functional asymptotic relate to the statistical performance in the large-width regime? iii) what is the connection between deep neural networks and random processes?

the following questions: What is the limit of a large-width neural network with fixed architecture and fixed number of hidden layers? What is the limit when the number of hidden layers is also allowed to diverge? What are the statistical properties of the limiting process?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a fully-connected feed-forward deep neural network with infinitely many neurons and weights and biases sampled independently from a zero-mean Gaussian distribution converges in distribution to a Gaussian process with continuous sample paths in the large-width regime, and that the limiting Gaussian process can be viewed as a Gaussian process prior over continuous functions on the input space.
infinitely wide deep Gaussian neural networks behave like continuous Gaussian processes with Hölder paths in the large-width functional limit.
a deep Gaussian neural network is a continuous Gaussian process with locally Hölder continuous paths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish that a neural network with re-scales weights converges weak to a continuous Gaussian Process in the limit of large width.

we show that the limiting Gaussian process of infinitely wide deep Gaussian networks with a suitable activation function is a continuous Gaussian process with almost surely locally Hölder paths, and the convergence rate is $1/\sqrt{n}$ where $n$ is the depth of the network.
, in the large-width regime, deep neural networks can be approximated by Gaussian processes with locally $\gamma$ Hölder continuous paths, where $\gamma$ depends on the activation function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the limiting continuous Gaussian process is a natural object to study in the large-width regime.

, under mild assumptions on the activation functions, the large-width limit of infinitely wide deep Gaussian neural networks is characterized by the same Gaussian processes as the ones studied in the literature on deep Gaussian processes (DGP).
the function-space perspective is a powerful tool to study deep neural networks and that Gaussian processes can serve as useful surrogates to approximate them.
